strategyReview: What is working: the house's YES-overpricing edge continues to show up in contract-aligned one-touch NO trades (clean live ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO 4/4, +18.4%/trade; gated FIND-0020 shadow 90/144, +2.0% avg; USER_PM_IV_TOUCH_RICH_NO shadow 9/10, +5.9% avg), weekend funding reversion is live-eligible (346/500 live, +0.31% avg; 188/253 shadows, +0.99% avg), and monotonic arb is live-eligible. What is failing: spot-direction hypotheses attached to contract/PM edge signals, shallow funding thresholds, HYPE/listed-IV momentum confirmation, and most Polymarket proxy-short families are burning capital and producing negative or breakeven shadow evidence.

failureClusters.evidence: FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG_PM_PROXY_SHORT 3/22 avg -2.85%; PC_RATIO_EXTREME_LOW_PM_PROXY_SHORT 1/16 avg -6.12%; OPT_IV_GT_PM_IV_DOWNSIDE 2/16 avg -9.95%; RELATIVE_VALUE_HEATMAP 4/15 avg -8.09%. These are spot/exam mismatches or weak proxy translations of a real Polymarket premium edge.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not promote proxy shorts. Either re-author them as contract premium fades with contract P&L predictions and proper directional neutrality, or leave them in shadow until contract-aligned.

failureClusters.theme: Shallow funding reversion thresholds without weekend/confirmation gates
failureClusters.evidence: CBRS H-539 13/27 (48%), AAPL H-537 10/20 (50%), MU H-535 5/16 (31%). Many failures show funding pinned at 5.5% or worsening from -4.3% to -33.8%, meaning the < -10 threshold fired on normal or already-decayed readings.
failureClusters.recommendation: Require true weekend timing, deeper funding stress (e.g. < -25%), and/or a 24h rise confirming reversal. Group these as asset-specific weekend variants instead of broad threshold tests.

failureClusters.theme: Spot-move predictions placed on contract premium trades
failureClusters.evidence: H-534 GOLD one-touch heatmap is 3/16 scorable with 6 unscorable tests; its primary prediction says GOLD spot declines >2%, but the evidence is contract P&L on NO. One winner was NO on GOLD above 6000 moving 0.795 to 0.865; tail NO on 7000 barely moved.
failureClusters.recommendation: Re-author contract edge families with contract P&L predictions and neutral direction. Never test a one-touch premium fade as a spot directional move.

failureClusters.theme: HYPE/listed-IV momentum confirmation is not independent
failureClusters.evidence: cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion 9/25 (36%), btc_listed_iv_momentum_confirmation 4/17 (24%). Repeated losses occur in strong BTC uptrends, and HYPE risk-on participation echoes the same beta tape rather than confirming durable BTC upside.
failureClusters.recommendation: Stop adding HYPE confirmation or rising listed-IV momentum variants. Replace with regime-relative filters that remove overextension, or abandon this spot direction line.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-534: treat GOLD above-strike one-touch NO as a contract premium fade, not a spot decline call. Require moderate underlying-cap edge, above-strike contracts, mid-priced YES ask, and near-dated expiry so the contract has room to decay without needing GOLD spot to crash.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on qualifying GOLD above-strike one-touch contracts is profitable over 7 days as the premium decays; no GOLD spot move is required.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-539: require true weekend timing, a deeper CBRS funding low, and a rising 24h funding change to avoid flat or worsening funding readings.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS spot gains >1% within 3 days as extreme weekend funding begins to normalize upward.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-108: remove the HYPE confirmation that was echoing late-stage BTC risk-on. Instead require BTC trend strength plus a non-extended PM IV regime and non-extreme funding.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot gains >1% within 3 days when short-term trend strength is present without PM IV overextension.

newHypotheses.description: Informed-flow asymmetry faded on near-dated mid-priced above-strike BTC one-touch contracts: when tracked smart wallets are net short YES, the dumb-money YES premium is overpriced and should decay.
newHypotheses.prediction: Selling YES / buying NO on qualifying BTC above-strike one-touch contracts is profitable over 7 days as dumb-money YES premium decays.

newHypotheses.description: BTC-specific one-touch NO premium fade with moderate sell-YES edge, above-strike contracts, tight spread, and meaningful liquidity to avoid stale or wide quotes.
newHypotheses.prediction: Selling YES / buying NO on qualifying BTC above-strike one-touch contracts is profitable over 3 days as the premium decays.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-539's raw condition only required CBRS funding < -10. Test outcomes show flat or worsening funding readings (2.3→1.3, -4.3→-33.8) and wins only when funding was deeply negative and reversed (-33.8→9.0). It was not weekend-gated and entered too early.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A standalone CBRS funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes within 2 days and forces a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-108-style BTC/HYPE confirmation produced only 36% family wins. HYPE spot above SMA with stable OI fired during the same broad risk-on tape and did not provide independent confirmation, leading to losses when BTC was already extended or reversed.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE risk-on participation independently confirms durable BTC upside rather than late-stage FOMO/overextension.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL funding < -10 was too shallow and not weekend-only. Outcomes show readings pinned at 5.5% or moving from 11.2% to 5.5%, meaning the signal captured normalized funding rather than extreme weekend stress. At 50% wins the edge is not separable from the base rate.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative AAPL funding (< -10%) rapidly normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain without requiring a true tail-event overshoot.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The BTC listed-IV momentum family is at 4/17 wins. Its tests were effectively short BTC and lost on +24.08% and +21.59% moves. Rising option IV was not a bearish timing signal; it appeared in strong uptrends and upside demand.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Spot momentum confirmed by rising options IV reliably leads to further >2% BTC gains within 3-7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-534 is 3/16 scorable with 6 unscorable tests because the primary prediction was for GOLD spot to decline >2%, while the evidence was collected on NO contract prices. Tail strikes like GOLD above 7000 NO near 0.94 barely moved; the winner was a closer above-6000 NO from 0.795 to 0.865. This is a contract premium fade, not spot direction.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on gold upside touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: MU funding < -10 produced only 31% wins. Most failures occurred because funding remained flat at 5.5% or moved from 29.1% to 3.4%, so the condition captured non-extreme or already-normalizing readings rather than deep weekend stress.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative MU funding (< -10%) outside true weekend hours rapidly normalizes and produces >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-551's OIL one-touch NO edge on the heatmap cluster is 100% over 33 scorable tests. This supports keeping the family alive when stated as contract P&L, not spot decline.

H-647 is 0% over 29 tests, confirming that rich PM IV on near-expiry OIL above-strike YES is not tradeable richness on its own; the PM IV richness is likely model error or stale pricing rather than overpriced contract premium.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Rich PM IV on near-expiry OIL above-strike one-touch YES implies premium decay within 3 days.

journalEntry: This run focused on diagnosing the struggling families rather than adding many new variants. The strongest lesson is still contract-vs-spot alignment: one-touch NO premium edges work when graded on the contract, but repeatedly fail when the prediction demands a spot move. Shallow funding thresholds also need weekend and reversal gates. No parameter updates were made because the current evidence does not cleanly support changing risk or timing settings.
